title: Non-sporting · the rest of the club
blurb: The utility shelf: breeds that guard, pull, sit on laps or simply refuse to be classified, from the French Bulldog to the Shiba Inu.

items.d: Parisian companion bulldog of the 1800s: 8–14 kg, bat ears and a sociable, low-energy manner.
English bull-baiting dog turned national mascot: heavy, 18–25 kg, and surprisingly gentle.
German water retriever refined in France, in three sizes; the Standard stands 45–60 cm.
Croatian carriage dog with spots, 19–32 kg, once run beside fire engines and coaches.
American bull-and-terrier cross from Boston: 5–11 kg, tuxedo-marked and snub-nosed.
Japanese mountain hunter, 33–43 cm, the smallest native breed and a national monument.
Mediterranean companion with a white curly coat, 5–10 kg, and a cheerful, sturdy build.
Tibetan monastery watchdog, 25–28 cm, with a heavy coat and an independent streak.
